newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Primary blue chips seen lifting Seoul stocks.
newsitem.headline: Primary blue chips seen lifting Seoul stocks.

text.p: Buying interest is expected to focus on primary blue chips on the eve of an expansion of the foreign share holding ceiling, brokers said on Wednesday.
The limit will be raised to 23 percent on Friday from 20 percent. The market will be closed on Thursday for Labour Day.
"Foreigners' favourites -- POSCO, Samsung Electronics and SK Telecom -- will be highlighted today ahead of the ceiling rise," said Park Key-pyong of Hanyang Securities.
The composite stock index closed on Tuesday at 704.05, down 0.11 percents.
Brokers said signs of an improving economy in indicators released on Tuesday would have little impact in the market.

Industrial output in March rose 9.1 percent year-on-year, up from a 5.8 percent rise a year earlier. The current account deficit widened to $2.27 billion in March from $940.2 million a year ago, but narrowed from February's $2.50 billion deficit.
Brokers said the market remained cautious about the troubled Jinro Group despite an 80.4 billion won bailout package.
